title: Facing funding barriers, euro zone firms use own cash for AI, ECB blog says
source_used: Reuters wire text via TradingView; ECB Blog post via Zpravy Kurzy.cz mirror
key_facts: An ECB blog post (2 Oct 2026) says euro zone firms mostly use their own cash to invest in AI and face funding barriers, unlike US tech giants that have borrowed heavily.
72% of firms planning AI investment expect to use internal funds such as cash flow or retained earnings; about 16% plan bank loans; 6% equity or venture capital; 1% debt securities.
Over 80% of firms plan to use just one financing instrument, mainly internal funds.

Firms are more likely to use outside funding for tangible assets such as hardware or data infrastructure, which can serve as collateral; intangible investment (for example staff training and specialists) is harder to finance.
The blog says the limited role of outside finance raises questions about barriers in the euro area's financial system; Reuters notes the blog does not necessarily represent the ECB's views.

The ECB blog bases this on its Survey on the Access to Finance of Enterprises (SAFE) of about 5,000 euro area firms; 49% plan AI technologies and tools, 46% staff training, 40% data infrastructure, 12% hiring AI specialists.
quote_evidence: The AI expansion in Europe is more modest, however, and 72% of firms say they will use internal funds such as cash flow or retained earnings to finance investment, the ECB said in a blog post.
"The limited role of external finance raises critical questions about potential barriers in the euro area’s financial ecosystem," the blog said
Firms are more likely to rely on external funding when they invest into tangible assets such as hardware or data infrastructure as these could be used as collateral, the blog added.
why_it_matters_hint: Europe's AI investment is being funded mostly from firms' own money, which may limit how fast cash-poor firms can invest.
notes: Reuters page returned 401. Reuters wire text read through TradingView's republication and checked against the ECB blog (mirrored at zpravy.kurzy.cz). Figures are firms' plans from a survey, not actual spending.
